records.claim: The pseudocode uses undefined list operations (append, length) which are too thin to implement.

records.why: The spec relies on undefined list helpers to collect available registers before random selection. The patch replaces these with inline counting to remove the undefined dependencies.

patch.value:
for b in 0 .. num_banks - 1:
  num_available = 0
  for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
    if (r % num_banks) == b and sR_InFlightState[branch.rob_index][r] == 1:
      num_available = num_available + 1
      
  if num_available > 0:
    chosen_idx = random_int() % num_available
    current_idx = 0
    chosen_reg = 0
    for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
      if (r % num_banks) == b and sR_InFlightState[branch.rob_index][r] == 1:
        if current_idx == chosen_idx:
          chosen_reg = r
        current_idx = current_idx + 1
        
    u_idx0 = hash_ut(PC, 0) % ut0_entries
    u_idx1 = hash_ut(PC, 1) % ut1_entries
    u_idx2 = hash_ut(PC, 2) % ut2_entries
    
    u_delta = calculate_utility_delta(branch)
    sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    
    digest = sR_RegTable[chosen_reg].payload
    w_idx0 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 0) % wt0_entries
    w_idx1 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 1) % wt1_entries
    w_idx2 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 2) % wt2_entries
    
    w_delta = 1 if branch.direction == 1 else -1
    sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] = saturate(sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] + w_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] = saturate(sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] + w_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2] = saturate(sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2] + w_delta, wt_bits)

patch.value: Table 3 of the paper claims 53863 bits for sR. My total is 70503 bits. I am over by 16640 bits. The paper's total exactly covers WT, UT, and RegTable (43008 + 9360 + 1495 = 53863). It omits the 16640 bits needed for sR_InFlightState to snapshot the 65 valid bits per in-flight branch, which the update algorithm requires to know which registers were available at prediction time. Naming the host as the provider does not remove this from the budget at iso-storage. The 'val' variable is provided by the host exactly at instruction completion when the digest is generated, so it is not carried from prediction and consumes no storage budget.
